Definition: A covenant — a solemn, binding promise and relationship, often sealed with sacrifice, signs and blessings and curses.
BiblicalUsage: Berit structures the whole Bible story: covenants with Noah, Abraham, Israel, David and finally the new covenant in Christ. Each one is initiated by God's grace and calls for a faithful response.
TheologicalSignificance: Because God binds Himself by covenant, hope rests on His promise, not our performance. Berit is why believers can trust that God will finish what He began.
RelatedPeople: Noah; Abraham; Moses; King David; Jesus
RelatedEvents: Giving of the Law at Sinai; Davidic Covenant
